title: Goodman flies to Hungary for Contrasts
summary: Hammond arranged Benny's trip to Bartok, who wrote Contrasts.

story.theme_name: Working for Benny Goodman: the leader and his bands
story.community_name: Working for Benny Goodman: the perfectionist bandleader

blocks.x: Let's get onto that story you told me about when you met Bartok. I thought that was interesting.
It always has been
to me and it was an important moment in my life.
Benny, in 1938, flew to Hungary to meet Bartok.
Wow.
You didn't know that?
No, I didn't know that.
That's quite a journey.
That was arranged by John Hammond, and airplanes weren't that way. Of course Benny flew over Germany,--
Which I'm sure he was crazy about.
He admits to being frightened.
He got him to write a piece for him then.
'Contrast?'
'Contrast', yes.
What a good piece that is.
I think John Hammond engineere that through friends and Benny played with the Budapest string quartet. That all gets involved. Georgy Sandor was Hungarian--is, not was.
I don't think I'm familiar with his name.

I have an album downstairs, you can copy it if you'd like. Good piano player. Everybody was here, all the good musicians and all the great chefs came here during the war and it really did something for this country.
No question.

I'm sorry to see that period end because they all left. When the came they brought that culture with them, and that's the culture that's gone. The last of the greats; we've not produced genius of that type since then.
